title: The component model is written down before it is built
goal: Before anyone writes component code, the model detail has to be settled and written down: what a group and an instance actually store, how documents saved before any of this still open, and what must always be true so an edit to one component cannot corrupt the document. The product decisions are already written; this is the engineering half.
notes: The product-level IA is now decided and written: docs/design/ui-building.md (one tree, a frame is a group with a size, the Library is a panel group in the existing dock, a component is a subtree with instances pointing at it, styles are named values). Do NOT redo that. This task turns its component section into the model detail a runner can build from: the Codable shape of a group and an instance in PhotonzCore, how an old flat document decodes unchanged, what an instance stores versus what it resolves from its main, the invariants (an instance may not contain its own main, a variant may only pick among shapes the main holds), and how History.perform stays correct when an edit to a main changes every instance. Write it into docs/design/ui-building.md as a Model section, not a new file. Original note: Source material: docs/design/mocks/pages/component-configure-wt.html (the eleven step walkthrough is the whole flow: select the layers you drew, Make component, Add property, expose a toggle as a boolean, expose a control as a variant, bind a fill to a Style, drop an instance, configure it, reset it), components.html (the Library with scopes, drag to place), ui-variants.html (the variant by size matrix and instance props). The mock’s one line definition to build on: a component is a reusable layer tree with configurable properties, and nothing about it is a special editor. Where the app is today: PhotonzDocument holds one flat array of layers (Document.swift), LayerContent has image, text, annotation, zoomCallout, measure and collage cases (Layer.swift:324), there is no group, no library and no component anywhere in Sources. Copy the shape of docs/design/next-measure.md, which has served the measure epic well: numbered sections, a Done when list, and flags named next to the behavior they gate. Styles and tokens belong to the ui-design-systems epic, staged later, so the spec should name the seam and stop there.
acceptance: docs/design/next-components.md exists and covers, in plain language: a group, a main component, an instance, an override, a variant, where the Library lives, every menu item and key, and the flag each slice ships behind
It has a Done when section listing the slices in build order, each small enough for one working session
It states whether a child layer’s position is stored against its parent or against the whole picture, and why
It says what the first version does not do, so later work is not judged against a promise nobody made
It records where it disagrees with the mock pages and the reason
